Homebound
After a major storm hit the city, the
Shir family's plans quickly change
from an in-person concert to a
video presentation.Tatty, Dovid, and
Mendel are putting the final touches
to a lively version of כלאפצי זשוריטצי ניע.
They are getting really into it ... until
Esther Miriam interrupts. "I think we
should be called the 'Stuck-At-Home
Family,'" she grumbles. "This niggun is
all about traveling, but that's the last
thing we're doing in this crazy storm!"
Tatty becomes quiet and Esther
Miriam feels she has made a good
point. But thenTatty’s lips curve into a
smile. "That’s exactly what the niggun
is telling us! It’s a mashal: instead
of spending our time ‘traveling’ and
feeling unsettled in golus, we’re
supposed to be resting at the ‘inn,’
the place where the Rebbe is.When
we’re connected to him, we can enjoy
some ‘l'chayim,’ which is the spiritual
nourishment he gives.
“Esther Miriam, our family is at the
‘inn’ right now!Through performing
this niggun at home,
we connect to the
Rebbe.”
Esther Miriam thinks
for a second. “I guess
that’s true...staying at
the ‘inn’ is important.
But I hope that by
the time the concert
comes around, we’ll
be traveling—with
Moshiach!”

Next Stop,
Tampa!
Tatty and Mommy were ready for
their own shlichus. But how would
they know where to go?
For two years,Tatty and Mommy joined our
uncle and aunt on shlichus at the University
of Maryland.
They loved it!They met Jewish students,
helped them learnTorah and do mitzvos, and
showed them the warmth ofYiddishkeit.
Time flew by quickly, and before they knew it,
the two years were almost over. It was time
to find their own permanent shlichus.
SoTatty and Mommy began asking around
and speaking to different people.They soon
heard about four different campuses that
needed shluchim. One of them was the
University of South Florida—called “USF”—in
Tampa, Florida.
USF sounded like a great place for them to
go on shlichus. ButTatty and Mommy still
weren’t completely sure.
Around Chof-Beis Shvat, תשס”ח (2008),Tatty
went to the Ohel. He wrote to the Rebbe and
asked for guidance: Which campus shlichus
should we choose?
After leaving the Ohel,Tatty went into the
room where the Rebbe video was playing.
It was a video from the Kinus Hashluchos in
תנש”א (1991).The Rebbe was saying a sicha to
the shluchos in the big shul of 770.
Tatty watched quietly.Then, suddenly, he saw
something that made his eyes grow wide.
There on the screen was Mommy, standing in
front of the crowd!
Of course, she wasn’t Mommy yet. She was
a little girl then, visiting the Rebbe with her
mother, Mrs. Ruth Cohen.They had come
from Leeds, England, where their family was
on shlichus.
Tatty stared in shock. Wait a minute, he
thought. Mommy told me that she only came
to the Rebbe once as a little girl. It was for the
Kinus Hashluchos in תנש”א.
And now, right after he had asked the Rebbe
where they should go on shlichus, that
very video was playing in front
of him!
Tatty could hardly believe
it. Out of all the Rebbe
videos that could have
been playing, he was
watching the one and only
video with Mommy in it.
Tatty felt that something
special was about to
happen. Holding his
breath, he watched

After the sicha, the Rebbe began giving
dollars to the shluchos. One shlucha
after another passed by, but JEM had put
background music, soTatty couldn’t hear
what they were saying.
Then the fifth shlucha came onto the screen.
It was Mrs. Sulha Dubrowski, a shlucha from
Tampa, Florida.
Just then, the background music became
quieter, andTatty could hear her words
clearly. “A bracha for the institutions in
Tampa, Florida,” Mrs. Dubrowski said to
the Rebbe.
The Rebbe answered, “Amen.”
Then the Rebbe gave her another two
dollars and said, “For the entire institution.
Much success.”
Tatty stood frozen in his spot.Tampa, Florida!
The very place that they were thinking about!
He understood that this was the Rebbe’s
answer.The Rebbe was showing them where
to go and giving a bracha for their shlichus.
And so, that summer,Tatty and Mommy
moved toTampa and started our Chabad
House at the University of South Florida.
From the very beginning, we knew that
our shlichus came with the Rebbe’s clear
guidance and bracha. And until today, we feel
the Rebbe’s brachos constantly, in every step
of our shlichus.
Sometimes, we also have questions.We don’t
always know which choice is right. But this
story reminds us that a Chossid can always
turn to the Rebbe and ask for guidance.
The Rebbe is with us, and he will find a way
to answer!

Do you know the answer to the title’s question?
It’s part of Yitzchak Avinu's bracha to his son, Yaakov: The
voices of Yiddishe children’s Torah and tefilla can defeat the
"hands of Eisav." This means that our learning and davening
have the power to overcome our enemies!
In the times of the Churban Beis Hamikdash, the children
knew that Torah was their best protection.When the Romans
surrounded Yerushalayim, they said, "If our enemies come to
fight us, we will go out against them with our ין ִ

children used to keep their place while learning Torah. The
Yiddishe children of that time knew how great the z’chus of their
learning was. They knew that with its power, they could defeat
anyone who wanted to destroy BneiYisroel!
And these were not older children above Bar Mitzvah; they didn’t
need michtavin in order to follow along. It was the younger children

The only thing I remember from
when I first met Sadyon is the
hunger, thirst, and heat. I had
been traveling on desert roads,
on the outskirts of the land of
the Plishtim,1
for weeks already.
Sadyon, a wanderer like me, was
also in desperate need of a decent
meal and a comfortable bed to
sleep in. He was the first person
to tell me the stories about the
man who they called Avraham.
“…Avraham, the man of kindness;
Avraham, the Prince of Hashem;2
Avraham, the man who would
help anyone and everyone…”
Sadyon could not stop praising
this Avraham.
The more people we met on our
travels, the more we heard about
Avraham’s greatness - and the
fonder we grew of him.
“They say he’s so generous that
the Malach of Chesed has nothing
to do when he’s around.”3
“He operates a hotel in the desert,
with free room and board, purely
to service others.”4
“Apparently he’s drawn tens of
thousands of people closer to
Hashem!”5
We decided to go to Be’er Sheva to
see for ourselves.6
We wanted to
meet this extraordinary human
being and see if everything that
we heard about him was indeed
true. But more importantly, we
decided to go because we were in
desperate need of food.
As we approached Be’er Sheva,
we smelled a delicious scent of
flowering fruit trees.7
Beautiful
orchards with hundreds of trees
soon came into view.We found
out later that Avraham had
planted all of those trees in order
to provide his guests with fresh
fruit.
After we continued walking, we
saw a unique tent in the distance,
covered in a cloud atop its roof.8
It looked like the most accessible
tent in the world, the only one I
had ever seen that allowed entry
from all four sides.9
And there
he was, Avraham himself,
standing at the entrance of
his tent!10
We stopped in our
tracks.We were taken aback and
overwhelmed by his impressive
appearance. He stood there,
scanning the area for guests,
eagerly on the lookout to help
someone. Like the sun,11
his face
shone with warmth and love.
The moment he spotted Sadyon
and me, he ran towards us and
begged us to give him the honor
of hosting.What followed was
probably the most pleasurable
experience of my life.
I had never before, and have
never since, received such service
from anyone. Anything we
asked for, we received;12
literally
anything. Avraham had huge
storehouses filled with all kinds
of delicacies, which we received
within moments of our requests.13
The bread was made from the
finest flour,14
we tasted the most
tender cuts of meat,15
and enjoyed the freshest of
fruits. Avraham served only the
best of the best for every one of
his guests.

Around Chof-Beis Shvat, ( תשס”ח2008), Tatty
went to the Ohel. He wrote to the Rebbe and
asked for guidance: Which campus shlichus
should we choose?

Tatty and Mommy were ready for
their own shlichus. But how would
they know where to go?

After leaving the Ohel, Tatty went into the
room where the Rebbe video was playing.

For two years, Tatty and Mommy joined our
uncle and aunt on shlichus at the University
of Maryland.

It was a video from the Kinus Hashluchos in
( תנש”א1991). The Rebbe was saying a sicha to
the shluchos in the big shul of 770.

They loved it! They met Jewish students,
helped them learn Torah and do mitzvos, and
showed them the warmth of Yiddishkeit.

Tatty watched quietly. Then, suddenly, he saw
something that made his eyes grow wide.

Time flew by quickly, and before they knew it,
the two years were almost over. It was time
to find their own permanent shlichus.
So Tatty and Mommy began asking around
and speaking to different people. They soon
heard about four different campuses that
needed shluchim. One of them was the
University of South Florida—called “USF”—in
Tampa, Florida.
USF sounded like a great place for them to
go on shlichus. But Tatty and Mommy still
weren’t completely sure.

There on the screen was Mommy, standing in
front of the crowd!
Of course, she wasn’t Mommy yet. She was
a little girl then, visiting the Rebbe with her
mother, Mrs. Ruth Cohen. They had come
from Leeds, England, where their family was
on shlichus.
Tatty stared in shock. Wait a minute, he
thought. Mommy told me that she only came
to the Rebbe once as a little girl. It was for the
Kinus Hashluchos in תנש”א.
And now, right after he had asked the Rebbe
where they should go on shlichus, that
very video was playing in front
of him!
Tatty could hardly believe
it. Out of all the Rebbe
videos that could have
been playing, he was

video with Mommy in it.

dollars to the shluchos. One shlucha
after another passed by, but JEM had put

answer. The Rebbe was showing them where

moved to Tampa and started our Chabad
